images.note: Real screen capture — the OLE DB Source Editor with Data access mode set to SQL command and an empty SQL command text box, plus Parameters/Build Query/Browse/Parse Query buttons. This is the exact screen and access mode the lesson's SalesOrderHeader/SalesOrderDetail join query gets typed into.
Real screen capture — the OLE DB Source Editor's Columns page, showing Available External Columns with checkboxes and the External Column / Output Column mapping grid below.

Real screen capture — the Derived Column Transformation Editor, with the Date/Time Functions folder expanded to YEAR(<date>) and a derived column named YearHD using the expression YEAR([HireDate]). Different source column and derived column name than the lesson's own DateKey/ExtendedAmount expressions, but the same editor, the same grid (Derived Column Name / Derived Column / Expression / Data Type), and the same YEAR() function this lesson's DateKey expression is built from — captioned accordingly, not claimed as a literal capture of the capstone package.

Real screen capture — the OLE DB Destination Editor's Mappings page, with the drag-to-map Available Input Columns / Available Destination Columns diagram and the Input Column / Destination Column grid below. Matches the lesson's final mapping step onto dbo.CapstoneFactOrderSales.

Real screen capture — a Data Flow tab after a successful run: green checkmarks on OLE DB Source and OLE DB Destination, with a row count on the path between them. This tutorial's data flow only has two components (source straight to destination); the capstone's own data flow runs through a Lookup and a Derived Column in between, but the same checkmark/row-count behavior appears on every path once a run succeeds — captioned accordingly.

imageSearchNotes: 47-capstone-building-a-real-etl-package/source-images/ already held 10 candidate images from an earlier, interrupted pass (oledbsrc-3..7.jpg, oledbdest-2..6.png) — all downloads from tutorialgateway.org's OLE DB Source and OLE DB Destination tutorials. Checked each with the Read tool: oledbsrc-3/4/7 and oledbdest-4/5/6 have the tutorial author's own hand-drawn red circles/checkmarks/boxes baked into the image (not unaltered, so skipped per policy). oledbsrc-5/6 and oledbdest-2/3 were clean (only a small text copyright watermark, no drawn annotation) and usable, but didn't cover the Columns or Mappings pages the lesson actually walks through, so the same tutorial pages' images 8 and 9 (not in the original leftover set) were pulled in too — confirmed as the same editor via the Read tool, no hand-drawn marks on either. A further search for the Derived Column Transformation Editor (no screenshot on any current or archived Microsoft Learn page) turned up tutorialgateway.org's SSIS YEAR Function walkthrough, whose first screenshot is a clean, unannotated capture of exactly that editor using the YEAR() function — the same function this lesson's DateKey expression is built from. Final five used cover every data flow component this lesson actually builds except the Lookup (already fully covered with its own four real screenshots in Chapter 4, Lesson 19, so not re-sourced here): OLE DB Source (SQL command entry, Columns mapping), Derived Column (expression editor), and OLE DB Destination (Mappings grid, post-run checkmarks).
